title: The People's Watch — shadow run of The People's Money rule
disclaimer: Unofficial shadow run of a candidate design described in The People's Money (Jamie Murray, 2026). It is not the design's formal 18-month rehearsal, executes nothing, and publishes no national issuance figure. Each live reading after the starting quarter uses the rule's inputs exactly as published on its computation date (the starting quarter's prices were read at launch; see interpretation 8); all data are fetched through the St. Louis Fed's FRED/ALFRED; the replay and the sentinels use current (revised) data. Whether the rule would keep prices stable has not been tested. Not financial advice.

interpretations_pending_review: CPI-U and the PCE price index have different base years, so each is measured as a log gap from its own epoch level and the two gaps are averaged.
The seasonally adjusted CPI-U (CPIAUCSL) is used; the book says CPI-U without specifying seasonal adjustment.
The annual path rate is turned into a quarterly step by compounding: (1 + a)^(1/4) - 1.
Computation dates are fixed at the 15th of the second month after each quarter ends (Feb 15, May 15, Aug 15, Nov 15).
Trend real growth is the arithmetic mean of the last ten annual percent changes in real GDP available on the computation date.

"As first released" is implemented as "as published on the computation date" (an ALFRED vintage, archived with fingerprints). Strict per-month first-release values are a Design Paper question. The starting quarter (2026-Q2) used data as published at launch.
Brake release 'within 1% of target' is read as a price gap of 1 log point or less.

Starting quarter (2026-Q2): its prices were read from data as published at launch (Nov 5, 2026), not the Aug 15, 2026 vintage. CPI-U is identical in both; PCE for Apr-Jun 2026 was revised down about 0.2% in BEA's September 2026 annual update. Anchoring to the Aug 15 vintage would build that statistical revision into the target permanently (about 0.1 log point on the overall gap). Open for review.
Which three months: the three months of the most recent complete calendar quarter (Jul-Sep for the Nov 15 reading), not the latest three monthly releases available on the computation date.

Real GDP: annual real GDP in chained dollars (BEA via FRED series GDPCA); annual percent changes are computed from these levels, not taken from the rounded percent changes in NIPA Table 1.1.1. A year's figure is first used from May 1 of the following year.

Frozen starting prices vs. later revisions: starting-quarter prices are frozen while each later reading uses its own vintage, so revisions to past months (CPI-U seasonal factors each February; PCE annual updates) can show up in later gaps. Alternatives: re-read the starting quarter from each new vintage, or use the not-seasonally-adjusted CPI-U, which is never revised.

Data access: rule inputs and most sentinel series are fetched through the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED and its archive ALFRED), which republish BLS, BEA and Federal Reserve data. Fingerprints prove what FRED served on the day, not what the original agency published.

backstop_proposal.operated_by: Treasury Exchange Stabilization Fund (successor to Fed swap lines per Ch. 8 table)
instruments: swap lines with central banks that already hold standing lines
repo against U.S. Treasury securities for foreign official accounts (FIMA-style)
open_questions: Is a cap of 20% of foreign official custody holdings large enough? It would have covered the 2020 swap peak (about $449B) but not the 2008 peak (about $583B).
Should the taper follow the calendar, the sentinel readings, or both?
Which central banks are eligible, and who decides?
Does the design need any rule about dollar deposits created by banks outside the United States, or only a backstop?

instruction.instruction: Raise the target path for public money by 0.611% this quarter (an annual rate of 2.466%). Issue only enough to close any shortfall below the path, in three monthly installments; if the stock is at or above the path, issue nothing. Brake OFF: no Stabilization Bill offer.
instruction.note: Shadow run: nothing is executed. No national dollar issuance figure is published until a reconciled model release supports one (Ch. 10).

report.headline: This quarter's result: three calculators agree, no brake needed, prices on track.
paragraphs: This is an unofficial shadow run of The People's Money issuance rule, run by The People's Watch. Nothing is executed. Think of it as a practice run that checks what the rule would have done, without touching any real money.

For 2026-Q2, the three calculators agreed. The price gap was 0, which means the price level sat right on its target path. The allowed growth along that path is 2.47% per year, or about 0.611% per quarter. The brake, a safety stop that would slow issuance if prices ran too hot, stayed off because it was not needed.

Some readings are marked as watch. One is a 13-week drop of 3.314% in Treasury securities held for foreign official accounts, flagged for human review. Another, the broad dollar index, rose about 0.576% over one month. Other stress and funding gauges read calm, like a thermostat reading near its set point.

The next computation is set for 2026-11-15, covering 2026-Q3 and using the July, August and September data. A replay of the rule starting in 2020-Q1 ran 23 quarters and shows how large gaps can get in a bad stretch, but this is a test, not proof. Whether the rule keeps prices stable has not been tested in the real world.
